# A program started with no window on screen puts one there with `open`, and
# only then. On gtk4 the Wayland protocol log says whether a toplevel was ever
# created: none without --open, one with it. fyne reaches the display through
# Xwayland, so its runs assert only that `open` ran and the program ended as
# written.
#
# testdata/window_open.txtar is the code.

[!headless] skip 'needs the headless compositor go tool verify provides'

[gtk4] sngl build --lang go --platform gtk4 -o gtk4 app.sngl
[gtk4] exec sh -c 'WAYLAND_DEBUG=1 ./gtk4/app 2>&1 | grep -c "xdg_toplevel.*set_title" || true'
[gtk4] stdout '^0$'
[gtk4] exec sh -c 'WAYLAND_DEBUG=1 ./gtk4/app --open 2>&1 | grep -c "xdg_toplevel.*set_title" || true'
[gtk4] ! stdout '^0$'

sngl build --lang go --platform fyne -o fyne app.sngl
exec ./fyne/app
exec ./fyne/app --open

-- app.sngl --
import go "sngl:language/go"
import time "sngl:time"
import ui "sngl:ui"

#[go.native("os", "os.Exit")]
func exit(code int)

output {
    go {
        gtk4(@run(args, run) {
            wanted = args.contains("--open")
        })
        fyne(@run(args, run) {
            wanted = args.contains("--open")
        })
    }
}

var (
    wanted = false
    ticks = 0
)

// The first tick opens the window when asked to, and the second ends the
// program -- so whether a window reached the screen is the whole difference
// between the two runs.
time.timer(interval=200ms, @tick {
    ticks += 1
    if ticks == 1 && wanted {
        details.open()
    }
    if ticks == 2 {
        exit(0)
    }
})

ui.window #details(title="Details") {
    ui.text(value="{ticks}")
    ui.button(text="Close", @click {
        details.close()
    })
}
